'''Diana Harrison Wall''' (December 27, 1943 – March 25, 2024) was an American [[environmental scientist]] and [[soil ecologist]]. She was the founding director of the School of Global Environmental Sustainability,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://sustainability.colostate.edu/about/leadership|title=SoGES Leadership|publisher=School of Global Environmental Sustainability|access-date=May 21, 2014}}</ref> a distinguished biology professor, and senior research scientist at the Natural Resource Ecology Laboratory at [[Colorado State University]]. Wall investigated ecosystem processes, [[soil biodiversity]] and [[ecosystem service]]s. Her research focused on the [[Antarctic]] [[McMurdo Dry Valleys]] and its [[Wall Valley]] was named after her. Wall was a globally recognized leader and speaker on [[Wildlife of Antarctica|life in Antarctica]] and [[climate change]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.coloradoan.com/story/life/2014/04/26/diana-wall-research-star-born-star-antarctica/8191289/|title=Diana Wall: A research star is born star in Antarctica|last=Handy|first=Ryan Maye|date=April 29, 2014|newspaper=The Coloradoan|access-date=May 22, 2014}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=http://www.britishecologicalsociety.org/grants-awards/honours_awards_prizes/tansley-lecture/|title=Tansley Lecture|website=www.britishecologicalsociety.org|publisher=British Ecological Society|access-date=June 2, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160526140606/http://www.britishecologicalsociety.org/grants-awards/honours_awards_prizes/tansley-lecture/|archive-date=May 26, 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{cite web |last1=Jeracki |first1=Kate |url=https://source.colostate.edu/udp-diana-wall-receives-2015-ulysses-medal/ |title=UDP Diana Wall receives 2015 Ulysses Medal |date=June 16, 2015 |publisher=[[Colorado State University]] |language=en-US |access-date=April 1, 2024 }}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Diana Wall was born on December 27, 1943,<ref>{{cite web |title=Diana H. Wall |url=https://www.nasonline.org/directory-entry/diana-harrison-wall-jzis1v/ |publisher=National Academy of Sciences |access-date=April 1, 2024}}</ref> in [[Durham, North Carolina]].<ref name="NAS">{{cite web |title=Diana H. Wall |url=https://www.nasonline.org/member-directory/members/13054.html |publisher=National Academy of Sciences |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190324142358/https://www.nasonline.org/member-directory/members/13054.html |archive-date=March 24, 2019 |url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name=":4">{{Cite journal |last=Bardgett |first=Richard D. |date=2024-05-23 |title=Diana Wall obituary: ecologist who foresaw the importance of soil biodiversity |journal=Nature |language=en |volume=629 |issue=8013 |pages=754 |doi=10.1038/d41586-024-01414-9 |bibcode=2024Natur.629..754B |issn=0028-0836|doi-access=free }}</ref> Her formative years were spent in [[Lexington, Kentucky]], where she graduated from [[Lafayette High School (Kentucky)|Lafayette High School]]. She earned a Bachelor of Arts in biology from the [[University of Kentucky]] in 1965.<ref name="NAS"/> Her interest in [[nematode]]s began during her undergraduate studies when she worked on nematode parasites in horses and birds. She completed her PhD in [[plant pathology]] from the University of Kentucky in 1971.<ref name=":2">{{cite web |url=http://tylerprize.usc.edu/laureates/tyler2013.html |website=[[Tyler Prize for Environmental Achievement]] |title=2013 Tyler Laureate: Diana H. Wall |access-date=April 1, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160605091702/http://tylerprize.usc.edu/laureates/tyler2013.html |archive-date=June 5, 2016 |format=web.archive.org |url-status=dead}}</ref>

== Career and impact ==
Wall began work as a postdoctoral researcher at [[University of California, Riverside|University of California-Riverside]] in 1972 where she researched the function and biological diversity of soil ecosystems.<ref name=":2" /> In 1976 she began work in the Department of Nematology as an Assistant Research [[Nematologist]]. She continued to work at UC Riverside for a further seventeen years before becoming a Professor in the Department of Nematology. Throughout this period, she was the Associate Director of the Drylands Research Institute from 1986 to 1988 and the Associate Program Director of the [[National Science Foundation]] in Washington, DC, from 1988 to 1989.<ref name="CV">{{cite web |title=Diana Harrison Wall |url=https://walllab.colostate.edu/wp-content/uploads/2021/07/CURRICULUM-VITAE_06_08_2021.pdf |publisher=Colorado State University |date=July 22, 2021}}</ref>

Wall began working at [[Colorado State University]] in 1993. At this time, she became a Professor in the Department of Forest, Rangeland, and Watershed Stewardship (until 2006), the Associate Dean for Research in the Natural Resources College (until 2000) and the Director of the Natural Resource Ecology Laboratory (until 2005).<ref name=":2" /> Wall became a Professor in the Department of Biology at CSU in 2006 and was key in establishing the School of Global Environmental Sustainability at CSU in 2008.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://sustainability.colostate.edu/about/people/diana-wall|title=Diana H. Wall |publisher=School of Global Environmental Sustainability|access-date=June 3, 2016}}</ref>

Wall began working in Antarctica's [[McMurdo Dry Valleys|Dry Valleys]] in 1989.<ref name="CSU News">{{Cite web |first=Nik |last=Olsen|title=Diana Wall, groundbreaking soil ecologist who left a lifetime legacy at Colorado State University |url=https://source.colostate.edu/diana-wall/ |publisher=Colorado State University News |date=March 26, 2024 |access-date=March 29, 2024}}</ref> She conducted long-term soil ecology research in the region, drawing links between soil process and diversity to environmental conditions. Wall played a key role in pioneering the study and measurement of [[anhydrobiosis]], which is how nematodes cope physiologically with dry and hot temperatures.<ref name=":5" /> Specifically, she found that ''Scottnema lindsayae'' play a big role in the carbon cycle in the valleys.<ref name=":4" /> She described invertebrate soil communities in the Dry Valleys of [[Victoria Land]] and devised some of the first models of habitat suitability for specific invertebrate species in the Dry Valleys, which increased our understanding of their susceptibility to environmental change and their roles in biogeochemical processes.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Porazinska |first1=Dorota L. |last2=Wall |first2=Diana H. |last3=Virginia |first3=Ross A. |title=Invertebrates in ornithogenic soils on Ross Island, Antarctica |journal=Polar Biology |date=August 2002 |volume=25 |issue=8 |pages=569–574 |doi=10.1007/s00300-002-0386-7 |bibcode=2002PoBio..25..569P |url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/227184348}}</ref><ref name=":5" /> 

Wall served as president of the [[American Institute of Biological Sciences]], the [[Ecological Society of America]],<ref>{{cite web |last1=White |first1=Sally |title=Diana Wall, Soil Ecologist |url=https://www.esa.org/history/2016/03/wall-diana/ |publisher=Ecological Society of America |date=March 14, 2016}}</ref> the Association of Ecosystem Research Centers, and the Society of Nematologists. Wall also served as the Chair of the Council of Scientific Society Presidents in 2003 and in 2011 was appointed the Chair of the [[Global Soil Biodiversity Initiative]].<ref>{{cite web |title=President's Medal for Outstanding Achievement in Antarctic Science Diana Wall |url=https://scar.org/~documents/capacity-building/medals/wall-citation-2012?layout=default |publisher=Scientific Committee on Antarctic Research |date=July 2012}}</ref><ref name=":4" /> She was elected a member of the [[National Academy of Sciences]] in 2018.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Guiden |first1=Mary |title=Soil ecologist Diana Wall named to National Academy of Sciences |url=https://natsci.source.colostate.edu/soil-ecologist-diana-wall-named-to-national-academy-of-sciences/ |publisher=Colorado State University |date=May 2018}}</ref>

== Awards and honors ==
[[File:Wall_Valley_Antarctica.png|thumb|[[Wall Valley]], Antarctica]]
Wall received the 2012 Mines Medal from the [[South Dakota School of Mines and Technology]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://rapidcityjournal.com/news/colorado-ecologist-awarded-mines-medalist/article_266409c2-2e63-5f92-8915-4de73d7fbc5f.html|title=Colorado ecologist awarded 2012 Mines Medalist|last=Cook|first=Andrea |website=Rapid City Journal|date=September 28, 2012 |access-date=May 31, 2016}}</ref> the [[SCAR medal|Scientific Committee for Antarctic Research President's Medal]] for Excellence in Antarctic Research,<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.scar.org/scar_media/documents/awards/medals/Wall_Citation_2012.pdf|title=President's Medal for Outstanding Achievement in Antarctic Science|date=2012|website=scar.org|access-date=May 31, 2016}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.scar.org/scar_media/documents/awards/medals/Wall_Response_2012.pdf|title=Wall's Response to Receiving the SCAR Medal|last=Wall|first=Diana|date=2012|website=scar.org|access-date=June 6, 2016|archive-date=January 23, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170123074906/http://www.scar.org/scar_media/documents/awards/medals/Wall_Response_2012.pdf|url-status=dead}}</ref> and the Soil Ecology Society Professional Achievement Award.<ref name="CV"/>

Wall was named a Fellow of the Aldo Leopold Leadership Program in 1999. She was selected as the 2012 Tansley Lecturer of the [[British Ecological Society]].<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.amazonia.org/Documents/7.htm|title=DIVERSITAS-International Biodiversity Observation Year(IBOY)|website=www.amazonia.org|access-date=May 31, 2016}}</ref> She was one of the inaugural Fellows of the [[Ecological Society of America]] in 2012.<ref>{{Cite web |title=ESA Fellows |url=https://esa.org/about/awards/fellows-program/esa-fellows/ |access-date=2025-08-13 |website=Ecological Society of America}}</ref>

Wall was awarded the [[Tyler Prize for Environmental Achievement|Tyler Prize]] for Environmental Achievement in 2013<ref name=":2"/> and was inducted into the [[Colorado Women's Hall of Fame]] in 2014.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.denverpost.com/business/ci_25347730/colorado-womens-hall-fame-induct-class-2014-thursday|title=Colorado Women's Hall of Fame to induct class of 2014|last=Painter|first=Kristen Leigh|newspaper=Denver Post|publication-date=2014}}</ref><ref name="CWHF">{{cite web |title=Diana H. Wall, PhD |url=https://www.cogreatwomen.org/project/diana-h-wall/ |website=Colorado Women's Hall of Fame |access-date=April 1, 2024}}</ref> She was elected to the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]]<ref name=":3">{{cite web|url=http://www.news.colostate.edu/Release/7264|title=Diana Wall of Colorado State University elected to American Academy of Arts and Sciences|publisher=Colorado State University|access-date=May 21, 2014}}</ref> and named a [[Fellow of the American Association for the Advancement of Science]] in 2014.<ref name=":3" /> Wall was awarded [[University College Dublin]]'s highest honour, the Ulysses Medal, in 2015.<ref name=":1" />

[[Wall Valley]] in the [[McMurdo Dry Valleys]] of Antarctica was named for her due to her extensive research on [[soil biology]], including spending 13 field seasons there at the time of the naming.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://wp.natsci.colostate.edu/walllab/research/antarctica/wall-valley-antarctica-information/ |title=Wall Valley, Antarctica information |website=Soil Biodiversity and Ecosystem Functioning Lab |publisher=Department of Biology at Colorado State University |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190702102818/http://wp.natsci.colostate.edu/walllab/research/antarctica/wall-valley-antarctica-information/ |archive-date=July 2, 2019 |format=web.archive.org |access-date=April 1, 2024 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Antarctica Detail: Antarctica ID: 18663 |url=https://geonames.usgs.gov/apex/f?p=gnispq:5:::NO::P5_ANTAR_ID:18663 |publisher=[[United States Geological Survey|U.S. Geological Survey]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210602214257/https://geonames.usgs.gov/apex/f?p=gnispq:5:::NO::P5_ANTAR_ID:18663 |archive-date=June 2, 2021 |format=web.archive.org |quote=An upland valley next E of Priscu Valley in Olympus Range; Minotaur Pass is at the head between Apollo Peak and Mount Electra. The valley opens N to McKelvey Valley. Named by Advisory Committee on Antarctic Names (US-ACAN) (2004) after Diana Wall, Natural Resources Ecology Laboratory, Colorado State University, Fort Collins, CO; U.S. Antarctic Project (USAP) soils biologist in the McMurdo Dry Valleys, 13 field seasons, 1989–2002.}}</ref>

== Other activities ==
Wall chaired the DIVERSITAS-International Biodiversity Observation (2001–2002) and the Global Litter Invertebrate Decomposition Experiment.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Wall|first1=Diana H.|last2=Bradford|first2=Mark A.|last3=St. John|first3=Mark G.|last4=Trofymow|first4=John A.|last5=Behan-Pelletier|first5=Valerie|last6=Bignell|first6=David E.|last7=Dangerfield|first7=J. Mark|last8=Parton|first8=William J.|last9=Rusek|first9=Josef|date=November 1, 2008|title=Global decomposition experiment shows soil animal impacts on decomposition are climate-dependent|journal=Global Change Biology|language=en|volume=14|issue=11|pages=2661–2677|doi=10.1111/j.1365-2486.2008.01672.x|issn=1365-2486|pmc=3597247|bibcode=2008GCBio..14.2661W}}</ref> She also co-chaired the Millennium Development Goals Committee of the [[Millennium Ecosystem Assessment]] and the AAAS panel for the What We Know initiative from 2013 to 2014.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://whatweknow.aaas.org/about-the-initiative/the-panel/|title=The Panel|website=What We Know|language=en-US|access-date=May 31, 2016}}</ref> Wall was a member of one of the [[President's Council of Advisors on Science and Technology]] (PCAST) working groups and a member of the [[UNESCO]] International Hydrological Program US National Committee. She was a board member of the [[Island Press]] and the [[World Resources Institute]].<ref name="CWHF"/>

Wall died on March 25, 2024.<ref name="CSU News"/><ref name="Coloradoan">{{cite news |last1=Lyell |first1=Kelly |date=March 27, 2024 |title=CSU professor Diana Wall, a leader in environmental science and sustainability, has died |url=https://www.coloradoan.com/story/news/education/2024/03/27/colorado-state-university-professor-well-known-environmental-scientist-diana-wall-has-died/73123422007/ |url-access=subscription |work=Coloradoan}}</ref><ref name=":5">{{CiteQ|Q126162856}}</ref>
